newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares bounce off lows on bargain buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares bounce off lows on bargain buying.

text.p: Singapore blue chips ended down but off their lows in a flurry of late bargain hunting on Thursday.

"Some buying came back just before the close for a few of the blue chips like Keppel Corp, CityDev and SIA foreign. There could have been some last minute short covering ahead of the budget," said a broker with a Singapore firm.
The Singapore budget is due on Friday afternoon.

Buying was not aggressive and most shares closed weaker, pulling the 30-share Straits Times Industrial Index (STI) down 14.63 points at 1,968.34, but not before it made a new 30-month low of 1,956.21 in intra-day trade.
Singapore Press foreign topped the losers' list, ending down Singapore $1.20 at S$28.30. The foreign tranches of DBS Bank and UOB Bank also shed 50 cents to S$19 and 40 cents to S$15.10 respectively.
"Sentiment in the afternoon was really pulled down by the weak Malaysian market. Any sharp fall in markets there does affect sentiment here as the markets are linked," said a dealer.
Malaysian issues traded over the counter, as measured by the UOB-OTC index, closed down 1.60 percent or 17.89 points at 1,099.88 on the back of concerns over the direction of the ringgit.

"Funds seem very concern about the weakness of the regional currencies and the speculation going on, so many are just not buying. Others who have positions are cutting them because of this uncertainty," said the dealer.
